exposure: Newborns delivered by non-elective caesarean section
outcome: Maternal vaginal microbiome composition and diversity
Newborn skin microbiome composition and diversity
Newborn oral microbiome composition and diversity
cohort: 58 mother-baby dyads, all consecutive primiparous women with a physiological pregnancy and term labour
finding: Duration of rupture of membranes was the single most important factor influencing the composition and diversity of maternal vaginal, newborn oral, and newborn skin microbiomes, with longer durations associated with a decrease in Lactobacillus and an increase in genera implicated in nosocomial infections.
mod_finding: The effects of duration of rupture of membranes on the microbiome were also present in newborns delivered by non-elective caesarean section.
